answer: Each new agent seat must burn a physical pair: a shale chip and a sealed vial of that season's nectar, both listed in a one-use catalogue. Applicants photograph both beside the epoch glyph and report the vial's sugar reading on a refractometer. A bonded lab samples quartz grain spacing on the chip and the nectar's spectrum; both must match the catalogue entry, voided in the same transaction. A seat therefore consumes a real specimen, a real vial, and a paid lab check, so a thousand sybils would need a thousand matched pairs and a thousand funded verifications before the window shuts.
